en: Farmers use a long bamboo pole as a lever to pry large rocks out of their rice fields.
The rough bark of a Narra tree creates more friction than the smooth trunk of a banana plant.
The moon's gravitational pull creates the daily high and low tides observed along the coastlines of Palawan.
Black sand beaches in Ilocos contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that sticks to magnets.
Lightning is a large spark of static electricity that jumps between clouds or between a cloud and the ground.
Sunlight forms a rainbow when it refracts and reflects inside millions of spherical raindrops during a tropical rainstorm.
Fruit bats navigate through dark caves by emitting high-pitched sound waves and listening for the returning echoes.
Dark volcanic rocks around Taal Volcano absorb more solar heat during the day than the light-colored beach sand.
The flowing water of the Chico River possesses kinetic energy because of its continuous downstream motion.
Rufous hornbills use their large beaks as wedges to crack open hard nuts.
The slippery mucus covering a bangus fish reduces fluid friction, allowing it to swim faster through water.
Geothermal plants in Tiwi, Albay harness thermal energy from hot underground rocks to generate electricity.
